articleTitle: Position Control of a Parallel Mechanism Based Robotic Machining Bed
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Modern technologies enable rapid removal rates to perform the desired tasks in order to achieve better finish in less time. However, this rapid removal rate greatly sacrifices the accuracy of the workpiece being machined. In recent years, researchers have tried to find solutions to tackle this issue so that accurate results can be obtained. A six degrees of freedom (DOFs) robotic machining bed is such a solution which is capable enough to mitigate the errors faced in conventional machining processes and attain desired accuracy. Despite its advantages this system too faces some errors, one of which stems from the positioning of the workpiece. The aim of this paper is to mitigate this error by incorporating a PID controller with a 6 DOF robotic machining bed. The research presents a mechanical design of the robotic bed as well as its kinematic model to determine the key parameters affecting its performance. Dynamic modelling of the bed has also been carried out to determine the dynamic effects of the positioning errors. To minimize these dislocation errors being faced by the robotic bed a classical PID controller has been integrated and its gains are tuned to achieve the desired positional accuracy. The proposed control strategy has been verified through both simulation and experimental results to prove the effectiveness of the system.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of DenseNet121, VGG16, and Custom CNNs for Brain Tumor Classification using MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The categorization of brain tumors from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans is a condemnatory step in the identification and management of brain diseases. With develpment in machine learning and specially deep learning, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown impactful execution in the automatic identification of medical images. This paper compares three CNN-based models for classifying brain tumors: DenseNet121, VGG16, and a custom designed CNN. Both DenseNet121 and VGG16 utilize the power of transfer learning, while custom CNN is built from scratch for this specific task. The dataset used comprises MRI images categorized into glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumors, and no tumor. The models are evaluated on the basis of accuracy, loss, and generalization. The results reveal that DenseNet121 achieved an outstanding accuracy of 99%, VGG16 reached 98%, while the custom CNN yielded 96%. However, the custom CNN showed significant signs of overfitting during training, which will be thoroughly examined in this study. The paper further explores the benefits of transfer learning and discusses the tradeoffs in using pretrained models versus custom-built networks. This comparative analysis provides insights to the best practices to utilize deep learning models in medical image classification.

articleTitle: Gait-CNN21: A Two-Phase Human Gait Recognition Technique for Frontal View Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Security threats in different areas are the cause of main concern nowadays. Human gait recognition is one of the famous methods that address security threats by using the walking trait of a person for recognition. This is an efficient and robust technique but also has some factors, such as variations of clothing, carrying, and walking, that degrade the system's performance. To handle these factors, this paper proposes a new technique for human gait recognition called Gait-CNN21. The Gait-CNN21 is comprised of two phases that recognize a person using walking features. In Phase-1, a preprocessing technique is designed using four steps such as histogram equalization of the input image, normalization, augmentation, and Gaussian noise removal. Phase-2 is based on the design of a 21-layer CNN model and training the model using hyperparameters selected by extensive experiments. The Gait-CNN21 technique is evaluated by using frontal view data of the CASIA-B dataset and achieved the accuracy of 95.48%, 90.34%, and 89.44% on NM, BG, and CL, respectively. By comparing the results with existing techniques, it is evident that Gait-CNN21 obtained better results as compared to current schemes.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Smooth Real Twisting Sliding Mode Control for Dynamic Voltage Restorer in Mitigating Voltage Fluctuations
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The requirement for enhancing power quality in distribution systems has increased, which has improved the economically and technically efficient development of the power sectors. This research study addresses voltage sags/swells and related THD in secondary distribution systems by presenting a fused control approach for the Voltage Source Converters (VSCs) of a Dynamic Voltage Restorer (DVR). To successfully mitigate the effects of these power quality concerns, the control technique integrates Sliding Mode Control (SMC) with the Smooth Real-Twisting Algorithm (SRTA). The total harmonic distortion (THD) of a voltage disturbance may be detected and decreased by the smooth real twisting sliding mode controller (SRTSMC) in less than two milliseconds, and THD stays below 5% in all simulated scenarios, according to simulation experiments conducted using MATLAB/Simulink. Comparative analysis reveals that the suggested SRTSMC method outperforms the conventional SMC in terms of performance.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network Driven Electroencephalogram Characterization for Robust and Efficient Schizophrenia Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Complex psychiatric disorders such as Schizophrenia show symptoms like disorganized thinking and hallucinations, typically rooted in abnormal brain activity. Early detection of such abnormal brain activity significantly improves diagnosis and subsequent treatment. To that end, Electroencephalogram (EEG), a non-invasive technique that records electrical activity in the brain is often used to record information about these cerebral anomalies. EEG data can be analyzed using various techniques to facilitate Schizophrenia diagnosis. In that respect, traditional machine learning techniques have been extensively used. However, traditional machine learning techniques necessitate pre-processing and extensive feature extraction, which can often considerably vary from one dataset to another. In contrast, deep learning techniques are better suited to classify between normal and schizophrenic cases, owing to their sophisticated network architecture and their ability to resolve complex data. In this work, we leverage a convolutional neural network (CNN) to characterize EEG data from two cohorts to facilitate schizophrenia diagnosis. We report a 96.4% accuracy of classification with fewer network parameters which beats the current gold standard and shows promise for effective and robust detection and subsequent Schizophrenia diagnosis based on EEG data.

articleTitle: Real-Time Defogging using Dark Channel Prior for Enhanced Visibility
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The presence of fog is a notable obstacle for capturing images, particularly in the early morning hours. The diminished sight impedes the capacity to get distinct and comprehensive information from the surroundings. In order to tackle this issue, a rapid and live vision-based dehazing method is suggested. The objective of the technology is to dissipate the fog and enhance visual acuity. It does this by implementing four steps: using an exponential moving average filter to diminish the impact of noise and enhance clarity, preprocessing the filtered frames, detecting fog with the Gaussian blur technique, and applying the dark channel prior approach to achieve optimum contrast and remove fog. Comprehensive testing were carried out on live recordings to showcase the system's ability to significantly improve sight in different foggy situations. This technique demonstrates the superior performance in terms of following parameters like, an accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score compared to previous investigations. Our methodology achieved the greatest accuracy when compared to state-of-the-art transfer learning convolutional neural networks.

articleTitle: An Optimized Novel Hybrid CNN-Vision Transformer (ViT) Architecture for Brain Tumor Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Brain tumor is the uncontrolled division of mutated cells. If not detected and treated timely, it may ultimately cause death. According to data collected from different sources it is evident that, in past few decades brain tumor has badly affected a significant population worldwide and due to its expensive diagnostic and treatment strategies it has various associated socio-economic consequences. AI has played an important role in the medical imaging industry for the detection of various diseases. In this study a novel hybrid CNN-ViT architecture has been proposed for classification of Giloma, Pituitary and Meningioma tumors in a publicly available dataset ‘SARTAJ’. As compared to the conventional designed CNN architectures our proposed hybrid architecture achieved 98.1% accuracy. The proposed model has the potential to achieve the significant milestones in the medical imaging industry specially for detection of the brain tumors.

articleTitle: Hardware Development of IoT Based Solar Panel Cleaning System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Renewable energy is becoming the primary source of energy because of global warming, high prices of fuel and large capital investments. Solar PV system is gaining maximum of the market for residential, commercial and industrial consumers. PV panels require cleaning time and often to give maximum output. Manual cleaning become exhaustive when PV farms are on enormous scale. This research paper presents an IoT-based automatic solar panel cleaning system designed to mitigate efficiency losses caused by dust and dirt accumulation. By integrating advanced image processing, simulation, and control technologies, the system offers a robust solution for real-time monitoring and automated cleaning of solar panels. Utilizing a combination of MATLAB, Simulink, Arduino, AutoCAD, Fritzing, and Blynk, the system ensures optimal performance and maintenance of solar panels, thereby maximizing energy output and promoting sustainability.

articleTitle: Realizing Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare: Applications and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare is revolutionizing the clinical procedures in intervention, diagnosis, therapy, amelioration, eradication of diseases and other psychological and neurological diseases. AI has inevitably transformed the health diagnostics, because of the ability to produce improved and accurate results with better accuracy. It has become significant in recent era due to least requirement of equipment and low cost. Moreover, AI related techniques e.g., machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have also played their roles in improving the research and accurate outcomes in healthcare sector. This article presents a brief review about some major techniques of AI in the healthcare sector. Furthermore, some applications of AI relevant to this domain are also presented in this article.

articleTitle: Ideal Tilt Angle Calculation of Photovoltaic Module to Enhance Sindh Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Traditional electricity production techniques are costly, environmentally harmful, and need careful upkeep, shortage, and blackout of energy, especially in summer. Making utilization of the abundant renewable solar energy sources that offer a clean, green energy supply. One of the least expensive ways to generate energy is through solar power generation, which may be utilized as an off-grid or grid-connected system. The proposed location for the photovoltaic system coordinates of the Sukkur railway station in Sindh, Pakistan are latitude 27.700686° N and longitude 68.866813° E. To solve this problem, the current study created an efficient, robust, and eco-friendly Grid Tie PV System (GTPVS). Sindh is one place where solar energy has a lot of potential. Using an optimized seasonal tilt angle of range 2°–15° in the summer to meet the excess load demand of air conditioners and other air cooling systems, and 45°–50° in the winter to enhance solar power generation, average annual horizontal sun irradiation received on collector plane of solar module for the proposed location is 1943 kWh/m2/year, whereas annual average diffuse sun irradiation received on collector plane is 887.4 kWh/m2/year. PR, photovoltaic conversion and other losses, including inverter conversion efficiency losses, temperature conversion, and PV module efficiency, are computed in this study using “PVSyst Software.” The simulation findings demonstrate that, by employing optimum seasonal tilt angles rather than annual fixed tilt angles, which reduce solar systems' power generation capacity, the suggested Roof-Top Solar System (RTSPVS) design energy production is 972614 MWh/year. The suggested method has an Annual Performance Ratio (PR) of 84%. The current study is useful in Sindh province to receive maximum solar irradiation on the collector plane and meet peak demand of load in the day time.

articleTitle: Forecasting of Solar Power Potential in Pakistan Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: In power systems, renewable energy type, solar energy is significant in its present utilization and penetration; thus, there is a need for deterministic models for its forecasting. This work aims to develop an effective deep-learning model for predicting solar power potential in Pakistan, especially in the following cities: Lahore, Karachi, Peshawar, Quetta, and Islamabad. Three deep learning models, Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) were used to forecast the solar irradiance by using performance measures of root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and correlation coefficient (R) was employed. According to the results from different models, it is revealed that CNN outperformed all the models in most of the cities. In the case of Lahore city, CNN achieved RMSE 0.638, but ANN and LSTM achieved 0.0648 and 0.0638, respectively. The results indicated that CNN had a high level of performance and stability in all the studied cities; thus, it was the most suitable model for forecasting solar power in Pakistan.

articleTitle: A Reserved Pricing Mechanism for Nano/Peco Smart Grid Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: This work introduces a Nano/Pico smart grid energy market model where a market operator (MO) manages price determination for local peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading among distributed energy resource (DER) sellers and buyers. The MO determines trading prices based on reserved pricing models, factoring in the minimum and maximum price ranges proposed by sellers and buyers. In this framework, the MO calculates the supply-to-demand ratio (SDR) to classify the market into buyers', sellers', or equilibrium modes. The objective is to minimize buyers' bills or maximize sellers' revenues depending on the market mode. The model's effectiveness is evaluated using a dataset from a small community with five buyers and five sellers. Comparative analysis with existing methods demonstrates that the proposed model significantly enhances sellers' profitability and provides substantial savings for buyers. Through the simulation results it is worth noting that the proposed model increases the revenues of the sellers from 17% to 7% compared with the other state-of-the-art methods. Whereas, energy bills for the buyers can also be reduced from 24% to 12%. This percentage increase in revenues and reduction in energy bills validates the proposed model's efficiency and effectiveness compared to the other state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Study and Analysis of Different Compensation Circuits for PV Integrated Wireless Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Electrical engineering can undergo a significant transformation with the use of wireless power transfer, which does away with the need for traditional copper connections and current-carrying wires. Hence, Wireless Power Transmission (WPT) for short-range distances has gained attention in recent times. For WPT, radiative and non-radiative methods are used, whereas the non-radiative method uses inductive wireless power transmission mode. This mode results in a decrease in the efficiency of the system, for which compensation circuits are used. However, the selection of a proper compensation circuit needs considerable attention, as there are four types of compensation circuits: series-series, series-parallel, parallel-series, and parallel-parallel. In this research work, a PV integration WPT model is proposed for household applications in contrast to the traditional AC-supplied WPT system. The four types of compensation circuits are analyzed and compared for the proposed model based on the output current, output voltage, and output power. Whereas the model was implemented in SimulinkIMATLAB. It was observed that the parallel-parallel compensation circuit resulted in higher values of output voltage, output current, and output power as compared to other circuits.

articleTitle: A Distributive Hybrid Cell Balancing Technique for Series-Connected Lithium-Ion Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: As the demand for high energy density batteries has surged due to their use in transportation electrification and energy storage systems (ESS), the role of battery management systems (BMS) has become even more critical. Individual cells in a battery pack can develop imbalances in their state of charge (SOC) during charge/discharge operations, which in turn can diminish battery pack's ability to operate at its rated capacity. Therefore, cell balancing that ensures optimal performance of a battery pack becomes a critical function of the BMS. In this study, a distributive hybrid cell balancing technique is presented which incorporates both passive and active balancing strategies for optimal cell balancing based on the difference in SOC among the cells. The proposed method is designed to address imbalance in SOC more effectively and in a shorter duration compared to conventional inductor based active balancing and resistors based passive balancing. Simulations were run to validate the performance of the proposed technique during three different modes of battery operation: idle, charging, and discharging. Furthermore, a hardware prototype was also developed for practical demonstration of the proposed hybrid technique.

articleTitle: Analog Control Design for a Two Degrees of Freedom Bilateral Teleoperation System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: In this paper, we detail the process of designing and implementing a two-way teleoperation system in which the manipulators (master and slave) each have two degrees of freedom. Position-position architecture is implemented for both the joints on the master and slave manipulators. The controllers for both joints are implemented using operational amplifiers. The teleoperation system is tested for both free and contact motion. It is experimentally found that the joints of the slave manipulator follow the trajectory of the respective joints of the master manipulator. The slave manipulator also experiences force reflection whenever it comes into contact with the environment. The presented cost-effective setup can be used to introduce key concepts of haptics control technology to undergraduate students taking the course on linear control systems.

articleTitle: Identifying Appropriate Probability Density Function for Wind Speed Profiles of Two Coastal Cities in Pakistan for Better Wind Power Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: To assess the wind power potential of a specific wind site, a suitable distribution function that best suits the wind data needs to be known. In this study, we employ four probability density functions (PDFs), namely Weibull, Rayleigh, Log-Normal, and Gamma, on wind speed data obtained from two coastal cities in Pakistan, Gwadar and Karachi, to check which one is the best suited. Cities along the coastline of Pakistan offer greater wind speeds and, thus, greater wind power potential. The maximum likelihood technique is used to estimate the parameters of the density distributions. Three statistical measures-Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Coefficient of Determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>)-are used to assess the goodness of fit for every distribution. These measures give a complete picture of every distribution's correctness in terms of reflecting the recorded wind speed patterns. Numerical results reveal that the Weibull distribution fits well with the wind speeds of the two coastal cities compared to the other three probability distributions, providing insightful analysis for the evaluation of wind resources and possible local energy generation. The MATLAB environment is used to compare the distributions and validate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Optimized Control Techniques for Improved Type 1 Diabetes Health Outcomes
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Glucose, a simple sugar from dietary carbohydrates, is the primary energy source for cellular functions, including muscle movement and brain activity. The endocrine system reg-ulates glucose levels in the bloodstream to maintain physiological balance and health. Insulin administration, either orally or via an artificial pancreas (AP), utilizes control algorithms based on mathematical models to manage blood glucose levels (BGL). The extended Bergman minimal model (EBMM) is a sophisticated mathematical framework that accounts for fluctuations in insulin levels due to dietary intake or exercise-induced glucose utilization. Our research focuses on implementing Adaptive Backstepping Sliding Mode Control (AB-SMC), a nonlinear control strategy, to stabilize BGL in individuals with type 1 diabetes. This approach aims to manage fluctuations and maintain stability, enhancing health outcomes and quality of life. A key feature of this method is adaptive parameter estimation, which eliminates the need for precise model parameters during the design phase. The optimization of controller gains is achieved using a genetic algorithm, with the integral time absolute error as the objective function. Stability is ensured through Lyapunov control theory, confirming the controller's capacity for asymptotic stability. We assess the effectiveness of the proposed controllers through MAT-LAB/Simulink simulations, complemented by real-time hardware validation using a hardware-in-loop setup with the C2000 Delfino and MCU F28379D Launchpad. This combination of advanced control strategies and robust validation techniques represents a significant step towards more effective management of type 1 diabetes, promising improved patient outcomes and quality of life.

articleTitle: Active and Reactive Power Control in Asymmetrical Cascaded Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: This paper presents a 27-level multilevel inverter topology employing three H-Bridge modules in conjunction with high-efficiency power conversion. The proposed topology utilizes a cascaded configuration of single-phase H-Bridge inverters, following a 1:3:9 voltage ratio, to produce a 27-level staircase waveform. This grid-supporting inverter can supply reactive power as well as active power, and it has a smooth dynamic response and flexible management of reactive power. The design method is in line with grid compliance norms and improves overall power quality by ensuring minimal harmonic distortion. The modeling and simulation of a 600-kVA inverter have been developed, incorporating a liquid cooling system to enhance thermal management, achieving a high-power density of up to 25 kW/L and a full-load efficiency of 98%. The PLECS environment is used to simulate the proposed complete inverter system under varying conditions. The topology is adaptable for varied power ratings and allows great scalability, according to detailed analysis, making it versatile for a variety of renewable energy and industrial applications. The inverter might greatly enhance the present energy infrastructure and grid stability, as shown by its effective deployment and performance results.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing based Human Monitoring and Recognition over Public Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Due to the ability to capture data from such distinct aerial perspectives, UAVs have gained numerous applications in drone imaging, human action recognition (HAR), search and rescue (SAR), and surveillance. However, such applications have consequences such as complex backgrounds and partial occlusions. This research presents a unique technique to tackle these issues for HAR using drone video data. We present an approach beginning with frame extraction from drone footage and preprocessing. First, we perform gamma correction and then we conduct background subtraction. YOLO detects humans, and key point extraction is achieved by extracting the important human joint points. The features were extracted, including full body features acquired by SIFT and LBP, key point features via spin images, and the Unique Shape Context (USC). Next, we improve these features using linear discriminant analysis (LDA), followed by a neuro-fuzzy classifier. The accuracy was assessed on the UAV Human and Drone Action datasets with scores of 56.4% and 86.7%, respectively.

articleTitle: Robust Spoofing Detection in GNSS-SDR Systems: A Two-Stage Method for Real-Time Signal Integrity
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Securing Global Navigation Satellite System Software-Defined Radio (GNSS-SDR) systems against spoofing attacks is crucial for maintaining the integrity and reliability of positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) services. Despite advancements in spoofing detection methods, a significant research gap remains in developing effective and efficient techniques that operate in real-time under various conditions. This study addresses this gap by proposing a two-stage spoofing detection technique that integrates In-Band Signal Strength Monitoring (IBSSM) during the acquisition stage and Carrier-to-Noise Density Ratio C/N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> monitoring during the tracking stage. The proposed methodology employs the Texas Spoofing Test Battery (TEXBAT) datasets, which include GPS L1 C/A signals under both static and dynamic conditions, to evaluate the performance of the detection system. Key findings indicate that the two-stage detection mechanism significantly improves the detection of spoofing attacks, demonstrating enhanced robustness against sophisticated threats. The implications of this research underscore the necessity of incorporating comprehensive spoofing detection methodologies in modern GNSS-SDR systems, particularly in critical applications where security and reliability are paramount.

articleTitle: Optimal Selection of Trading Partner in Peer-to-Peer Energy Markets
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Peer-to-Peer (P2P) energy trading in smart grids offers a promising solution to mitigate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$CO_2$</tex> emissions. The success of a P2P energy market hinges on participants' involvement, which is significantly influenced by effective trading partner selection that ensures both energy bill savings for buyers and profitability for sellers. This paper proposes a model that optimizes trading partner selection to enhance participant utilities. The model considers various factors, including prices, quality of energy, confidence in energy delivery, and the supply-to-demand ratio (SDR). Our approach evaluates 11 energy sellers (ESs) and 11 energy consumers (ECs) over a one-year dataset, comparing the proposed model with an existing model from the literature. Results demonstrate that our model increases both revenue for ESs and savings in energy bills for ECs, outperforming the benchmark model. This study underscores the importance of optimal trading partner selection in achieving fair and efficient energy markets, ultimately contributing to the broader goal of sustainable energy management.

articleTitle: A Novel Sports Event Recognition using Pose Estimation and Multi-Fused Features
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Several factors, including the dimension and locus of the limbs and head, and other pictures within an environment, were used to determine the management of event identification and recognition in a sequential figure. Body parts were estimated in an attempt to observe and monitor people as far as they were involved in intricate situations. Several feature descriptors were used on both the skeleton points and the silhouettes: MSER, SURF; and BRIEF; as well as HOG. With this combination it becomes easier to increase the discriminative power of the extracted features; hence making identification more robust and efficient. The extracted features are therefore passed through a Random Forest classifier with an accompaniment of Particle Swarm Optimization as a pre-classifier. Performance analysis proved the proposed approach achieves an event detection accuracy of 85.7% on the UCF-50 video dataset. The results show that our proposed method performs better than existing event recognition methods, which makes our research a significant contribution to advancing the state-of-the-art in event recognition.

articleTitle: AI Driven Blockchain Reward Insights Using ML
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Several industries have embraced blockchain technology due to the change it has brought, especially in the way records are kept. However, one major problem inherent in the concept of blockchain from the participants perspective is the presence of unpredictable rewards in proof-of-work and proof- of-stake models. That is why this research aims at developing a new strategy to solve this problem by incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) as well as machine learning (ML) algorithms into blockchain compensation prediction. This project seeks to analyze how artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methods may be incorporated into blockchain technology to solve the problem of the unpredictability of rewards. Using the EtherScan API, we have obtained 1000 timestamps and block reward values, and for prediction of rewards for certain timestamps, we use the KNN algorithm, linear regression algorithm, and random forest regressor algorithm. Thus, a What We KNN attained an accuracy of performance specifies, and a random forest regressor attained an impression accuracy range of 74% particular timestamps. These outcomes show the benefits of advanced ML to the blockchain ecosystem as a tool that helps stakeholders make informed decisions concerning activities like mining, staking, or investing in blockchains with potentially high rewards.

articleTitle: Robust Human Pose Estimation and Action Recognition Over Multi-level Perceptron
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: This research proposes a novel method that combines human pose estimation (HPE) and sustainable event classification (SEC), focusing on skeleton and context-aware feature extraction for precise activity recognition through machine learning techniques. In contrast to traditional state-of-the-art approaches, our method improves posture and event identification in daily activities by integrating individual detection, skeletal structure creation, and advanced feature extraction methods. The process begins with video-to-image conversion, followed by sliding window application for gradient-magnitude images and background removal during preprocessing. Human detection is achieved using Otsu's thresholding, and key points are identified with the Shi-Tomasi algorithm. The pose estimation step generates human skeletonization, and feature extraction is performed using color histograms, Harris corner detection, and Speeded-Up Robust Features (SURF), optimized through Hill Climbing. Classification using a multi-level perceptron on the UCF-101 and Sports Videos in the Wild (SVW) datasets achieves accuracies of 86.9% and 86.7%, respectively. Our method's unique combination of advanced techniques represents a significant enhancement over existing solutions, with promising applications in areas such as augmented reality, service robotics, e-health, fitness, and security surveillance.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches to Forecast Ethereum Price Dynamics: An Evaluation Study
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Machine learning techniques have emerged as potential tools in the field of extensive research led by the growing interest in predicting the future price of Ethereum. This paper fills a major knowledge gap in the area by reviewing and analysing important literature on Ethereum price forecasting, with a focus on Ethereum and it is applicable on other cryptocurrencies as well. By using machine learning models, such as random forest and linear regression, this study fills the gap by comparing the models' ability to predict Ethereum prices properly and provides insightful information for researchers and investors. The implications of these results for the analysis of the cryptocurrency market are noteworthy, as they may reduce the risks associated with the erratic cryptocurrency market and open the door for more studies to improve prediction techniques in this ever-changing environment. The study emphasises flexibility and effectiveness in navigating complicated cryptocurrency marketplaces, which advances the understanding of machine learning applications in Ethereum price forecasting.

articleTitle: Robust Vehicle Detection and Tracking Model via Deep SORT Over Aerial Images
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Detecting vehicles is vital for traffic monitoring and surveillance which generally employ cameras on bridges or roadsides. However, aerial imagery offers greater flexibility by covering wider areas with mobile platforms. This study introduces a novel approach for vehicle detection and tracking in aerial image sequences, leveraging advanced image processing and deep learning techniques. Initially, images are preprocessed to reduce noise and enhance brightness using a Gaussian mixture model. For precise vehicle boundary delineation, image segmentation is performed using a Fully Convolutional Network (FCN). The Deep SORT algorithm is then employed for vehicle detection. The Maximally Stable Extremal Regions (MSER) algorithm is applied for vehicle matching to ensure consistent feature identification across frames. Vehicle counting is performed using deep learning-based methods, providing superior accuracy and scalability. Vehicle tracking is executed with the Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) framework, ensuring best performance and high precision. Finally, trajectories are drawn to visualize movement. This integrated pipeline demonstrates significant potential for enhancing real-world traffic management systems. The detection accuracy on UAVDT datasets reached 88%, with a tracking accuracy of 90% which shows superior performance.

articleTitle: Development of Novel- Epoxy-Based Transformer Bushing Insulator for High Breakdown Voltage (BDV)
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: In today's trends, nanocomposites have garnered significant interest due to their potential to enhance dielectric properties and be used as insulators. Incorporating nanoparticles into the base epoxy makes achieving highly efficient dielectric materials feasible. However, the low electric field stress management capability and insufficient relative permittivity of typical epoxy provide a hindrance. Efforts have been made to overcome these limitations by adding nanosized fillers with high relative permittivity to the epoxy to enhance the dielectric properties. This research study focuses on the development of Novel-Epoxy-Based Transformer Bushing Insulator using nanomaterial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Al}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiO}_{2}$</tex> • The epoxy resin served as the base material, with nano-fillers added to improve its dielectric properties. The hardener was added to initiate the curing process and create a highly crosslinked structure. Surfactants were introduced to improve the interaction between the epoxy resin and nanoparticles. The nano-silica and nano-alumina particles were combined in different ratio configurations to create the nanocomposites by using the preparation method; Sol-Gel and Green Synthesis, which were subsequently tested for their dielectric properties. The proposed sample is the nanocomposite made by the green synthesis method and with the combination of 0.3 g + 0.3 g of the nanoparticle. Results show improved dielectric strength of the proposed nanocomposites compared to conventional porcelain materials. This paper presents an environment friendly approach for developing epoxy-based transformer bushing insulators, offering enhanced performance.

articleTitle: Tuberculosis Detection in Chest X-Rays Using Hybrid Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Tuberculosis remains a big global health challenge, especially in areas with a lack of high-tech medical diagnostics. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning model for TB detection using chest X-ray images and associated radiological reports via a built model that combines CNNs, ANNs, and RNNs. It leverages strengths of CNNs in extracting spatial features from images, ANNs for the representation of complex relationships, and RNNs for processing sequential text data from reports. We use a diverse dataset comprising 2,800 TB-positive X-rays, 3,500 normal ones, and 700 publicly available ones to ensure robustness and generalization. The performance for the proposed model reached 97 precent with a precision of 0.85, recall of 0.90, and F1-score of 0.88 in the most challenging cases. The authors have also used the Grad-CAM technique to visualize important areas on the X-rays responsible for the TB diagnosis to enhance interpretability. Because of the model's capability of integrating image and textual data, it can detect TB very early with high precision, hence making it a good tool to deploy, particularly in settings where resources are limited and timely intervention is very important.

articleTitle: An Improved Method for Identifying SSVEP Single-Channel Target Frequency for BCI Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) is a brain response to flickering visual stimuli in the occipital area. SSVEP detection methods usually utilize multichannel configurations, which can be intricate and uncomfortable. Conversely, single-channel configurations are simple and user-friendly, but attaining the necessary accuracy is difficult, requiring the development of a reliable and accurate single-channel technique. For this purpose, this study introduces a hybrid VMD-LGBM approach to single-channel SSVEP detection. The proposed technique utilizes VMD as a preprocessor that decomposes the SSVEP signal into harmonic, intrinsic mode functions (IMFs), and noisy IMFs. To separate harmonic IMFs from noisy IMFs, the crest factor of the cross-correlation function was introduced. Then the restored SSVEP signal is used to extract features using power spectral density analysis (Welch's approach), followed by classification using a Light Gradient Boosting Machine. Our proposed approach performs better than available techniques in terms of classification accuracy and information transfer rate. The proposed single-channel approach provides better efficiency and user-friendliness for practical applications.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Sensors Fusion for Fall Detection and Action Recognition in Indoor Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: In computer vision and inertial sensors, recent research focuses on monitoring and identifying falls, as well as daily actions, through autonomous human action detection. In this paper, the proposed model utilizes multi-modal sensors for fall detection. The data from inertial sensors was filtered using a bilateral filter, known for its monotonic and maximum flat magnitude response in the passband, giving smoothness. Key properties, such as the Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) and parseval's energy, were retrieved. Additionally, fall detection was accomplished utilizing RGB (red-green-blue) videos, where features such as rectangles, triangles, full-body ridges, and full-body curves were generated. The final results from the inertial sensor and vision data were fused utilizing multimodal fusion. We then optimized the fused data using the Naive Bayes approach and trained Multi-layer perceptron (MLP) classifier for classification. The UR Fall Detection (URFD) dataset was utilized to evaluate the proposed system, demonstrating its usefulness by reaching an accuracy of 88%.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Brain Tumor Classification Using Texture and Statistical Features
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Identifying brain tumors possesses a challenging problem in medicine. Researchers typically use a range of traditional diagnostic techniques to increase diagnosis accuracy. However, these procedures can be costly and tedious. The study investigates how well machine learning methods such as SVM (Support Vector Machine), Decision Tree, Naïve Bayes, KNN (K-Nearest Neighbor), LDA (Linear Discriminant Analysis), Ensemble, and ANN (Artificial Neural Network) work for brain tumor diagnosis. Using the GLCM (gray-level co-occurrence matrix) technique, the evaluation function will be converted into numerical values to select appropriate attributes. The study utilizes texture, statistical, and combined feature extraction, as well as raw data without feature extraction, to determine the most accurate machine learning algorithm for identifying and categorizing brain tumors. Upon evaluation of performance, it is observed that the LDA outperformed the existing classifiers. Each algorithm's training time is also investigated. With 200 brain MR images for the study, utilizing the train-test split method, real set of data had training and testing subsets division in a 100:50 ratio. Data were split into both the training and test sets, with 67% allocated for training and test set of 33% for the first six mentioned algorithms. The labeled dataset for the ANN approach is split into three proportions: 70% for training, 15% for validation and 15% for testing.

articleTitle: Driving Like Humans: Leveraging Vision Large Language Models for Road Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Ensuring the safety and reliability of autonomous driving systems requires accurate detection and response to road anomalies. Traditional object detection methods have advanced in identifying predefined objects, such as vehicles, pedestrians, etc., but often fail with unexpected or unknown obstacles. This paper introduces a novel approach using Vision Large Language Models (VLLMs) to enhance the adaptability of object detection through natural language interactions. By integrating visual data with human-like text prompts, our proposed approach dynamically adjusts to new and unforeseen obstacles. Through extensive evaluations, we demonstrate that our VLLM-based framework is comparable to the state-of-the-art road anomaly detection models, underscoring the potential of VLLMs in autonomous driving.

articleTitle: A Robust Visually Secure Bit Plane Image Encryption Using Chaotic Map and SHA-512
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: With the introduction of the latest digital technologies, the protection of images from unauthorized use has become increasingly important, necessitating the development of robust image encryption techniques. This paper proposes a novel bit plane image encryption method that incorporates chaos theory and cryptographic hash functions. To ensure a high degree of security, the key for the three-dimensional Intertwining Logistic chaotic map is generated (initial conditions) using the SHA-512 hash algorithm. The chaotic map is then utilized to generate two random vectors and one random matrix, respectively. In order to shuffle the original bit plane structure, random vectors are used to scramble the pixel positions across the bit planes. A bitwise XOR operation is then performed on the shuffle bit planes with the third random matrix. To avoid the attention of potential hackers, a visually secured ciphertext image is generated by embedding the noise-like ciphertext within a host image. Several tests, such as histogram, correlation coefficient, key sensitivity, key space, entropy, Number of Pixel Change Rate (NPCR), and Unified Average Change Intensity (UACI), were performed on the proposed visually secured bit plane image encryption scheme. As a result of the extensive tests, one can conclude that the proposed scheme is robust and can withstand a wide range of possible cryptographic attacks.

articleTitle: Energy Management in Smart Grids: Innovative Solutions for Demand-Side Optimization Considering Control Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The paper delves into techniques to enhance energy management efficiency within microgrid systems, focusing on the Smart Grid context. With the progress in the global transition towards smarter and more sustainable electrical grids, Micro Grids have emerged as crucial elements, offering a decen-tralized generation of distribution capabilities within the broader framework of Smart Grids. Smart Grid management regarding the optimized utilization of different resources and energy storage while implementing grid control performances and regulatory standards is a critical priority in making Mi-crogrids work reliably and efficiently. The paper comprehen-sively presents relevant literature, exploring energy management techniques and outlining future research directions for maximizing demand-side management implementation by over-coming the associated challenges. Key considerations include demand side management, technical, economic, and regulatory obstacles, proposing solutions, and highlighting research gaps.

articleTitle: Enhancing Crop Yield Through IoT- Based Precision Agriculture: An Optimized Multi-Parameter System for Solar-Powered Tunnel Farming
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Agriculture is crucial for the economic development of our nation. As the human population continues to expand, we must take specific measures to meet future food demands. Soil remains the essential foundation for plant growth. Manual soil nutrient measurement methods are time-consuming, leading farmers to skip lab testing. This results in continuous cultivation of the same crop, depleting soil fertility. This paper delves into the execution of automation of tunnel farming & green house. Crop yield largely depends on soil fertility and moisture levels. Fertilizer recommendations are typically made based on the nutrients available in the soil. A system has been proposed to implement precision agriculture using Soil Integrated (NPK 7 in 1) sensor which measures Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, Electrical Conductivity, PH, Humidity and Temperature, Soil Moisture Sensor and Humidity & Temperature sensor for measuring of internal Temperature of control environment and the complete system is IoT based so sensor detects the parameters if there is deficiency of Nitrogen, Phosphorus and Potassium than controller gives instructions to pumps to operate and provides the respective fertilizer to soil so crop deficiency fulfilled. In case of low humidity in surrounding than motors start operating and control shed has been opened to maintain the humidity level. IoT enabled Smart farming enables growers and farmers to enhance productivity while minimizing resource wastage, including the judicious use of fertilizers to prevent environmental pollution caused by excessive usage. All real time parameters are visible on the digital display on a user-friendly interface designed for growers and farmers to easily interpret, helping them determine the optimal conditions for their plants.

articleTitle: Wireless and Voice-Controlled Automated 2-Wheel Drive Forklift for Enhanced Industrial Warehouse Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The automation technology is expected to become integrated into two-wheel drive forklifts, which is one of the fascinating growths in the rapidly growing forklift automation field. Forklift automation technologies have enhanced the management of material handling and warehouse operations in modern societies. Research has indicated that it enhances efficiency, security and productivity of a facility where it is applied. With it the industrial sector could be revolutionized by the reduction of labor costs, the minimization of the risks of accidents and the optimization of the utilization of space. Robotics, automation, IoT, and artificial intelligence will all be utilized for the manufacture of fully automated two-wheel drive forklifts. This technology enables forklifts to lift and transport pallets, load and unload cargo or transport goods within a given area. Forklifts designed with automation technologies interlinked and running do run safer and with less manpower input. To make operations using the forklift easy to perform, research efforts will focus on enhancing the use of advanced wireless communication technologies, Mobile Computing, and Speech Recognition. One of the primary controls that helps the customers to drive the forklift using their smart devices by sending instructions is through the application developed for the purpose. It is hands-free as speech recognition capability is also provided. Future expansions of voice and mobile controlled industrial automation systems are enabled by this program.

articleTitle: Reaching-Law Based Sliding Mode Control of a Stand-Alone Wind-Fed PMSG with Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: With the depletion of hydro-carbon based fuel, the world is shifting towards the renewable resources. The wind energy is a viable option as it is clean and abundantly available. However, there are challenges due to the stochastic nature of wind, such as power quality and voltage stability issues. In this paper, non-linear control is proposed to improve the voltage stability of the wind energy conversion system (WECS). An offshore wind turbine operating in stand-alone mode has been considered. The non-linear techniques used in this study are Sliding Mode Control (SMC), exponential (E-SMC) and power rate SMC (P-SMC). The controller makes the WECS insensitive to bounded disturbances. Two types of comparisons have been carried out in this paper. The first is between Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) control and Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC) for a typical wind profile. The second is between SMC, E-SMC and P-SMC. The simulation results have been performed in MATLAB/Simulink to demonstrate the superior performance of the power rate-based SMC.

articleTitle: Analysis of Factors Influencing Early Detection of Breast Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Carcinoma, particularly breast cancer, poses a formidable challenge, especially in Pakistan where it stands as the most prevalent cancer among women. This research investigates the complex landscape of breast cancer in Pakistan, utilizing a dataset from local hospitals. Through comprehensive statistical analyses and advanced machine learning techniques, including XGBoost and RandomForest, the study uncovers significant associations between socio-economic and psychological factors and the timing of breast cancer diagnosis among Pakistani women. Factors such as embarrassment, fear of treatment, and lack of awareness emerge as crucial determinants. The findings provide valuable insights for tailored interventions and contribute to the global fight against breast cancer.

articleTitle: Analyzing Hourly Energy Consumption Profiles of Commercial Buildings Through Statistical Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: High-resolution energy data are critical for optimizing energy systems in commercial buildings and integrating renewable energy sources. While detailed hourly energy consumption data are essential for aligning energy production with demand, most available data, such as monthly energy bills, lack the necessary granularity. Understanding customer consumption is crucial for assessing expected loads at strategic nodes and informing power system planning strategies. This study introduces an innovative mathematical method to derive hourly energy consumption profiles from readily available data sources. Unlike traditional methods requiring large datasets and statistical techniques, our approach is designed for simplicity and accessibility, particularly for the commercial sector. The methodology uses a mathematical reconstruction technique to transform aggregated data, such as monthly energy bills, into detailed hourly profiles. These profiles are based on a billing structure divided into three tariffs: weekdays, Saturdays, and Sundays. Key results show that energy consumption is highest during operational hours and lowest during non-operational hours, providing insight into load variation patterns. The method generated hourly load profiles over a year using actual load data from the distribution system operators (DSOs), effectively cap-turing energy consumption patterns during operational and non-operational hours across various periods and conditions. This approach enhances energy planning and management, supporting the integration of renewable energy into the commercial sector's energy mix.

articleTitle: Enhanced Human Interaction Recognition Framework using Pyramid Matching and Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The interaction of humans on images has been of interest in computer vision and pattern recognition. In fact, interaction recognition has become fertile ground for research in virtually all areas of research. Thus, proposing to use a Deep Neural Network to design an activity recognition system in that case. However, at the initial stages of the system, the integration of hue, saturation, intensity (HSI) color transformation brings clarity of the video frames. Additionally, filtering for noise interferences are used to minimize noise. Multiple Object Tracking (MOT) and statistical methods are used to extract silhouette. In the extraction procedure, we use the Texton maps, ORB (Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF), and Spatial pyramid matching (SPM) Method. Using Gray Wolf algorithm, we discriminate features and then identify the most meaningful independent content that describes the data structure. Finally, the DNN takes the last feature and dumps it into the human interaction zone. This approach is tested using the SBU Interaction dataset and achieves a recognition rate of 87% using the experimental method.

articleTitle: Optimizing Potato Disease Detection in Pakistan with Machine Learning: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The agricultural sector of Pakistan depends heavily on the production of potatoes, however diseases like Bacterial Wilt, Late Blight, and Early Blight are posing a growing danger to this industry since they can negatively affect crop productivity and food security. Detecting these illnesses using traditional methods is time-consuming, labor-intensive, and sometimes it requires specialized knowledge which is not easy for farmers. The implementation of a machine learning (ML) framework for illness identification using the methods of K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Random Forest (RF), Decision Tree (DT), Naive Bayes (NB), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Logistic Regression (LR) overcomes these challenges. This study utilizes data mining and preprocessing strategies to improve the accuracy of models and adaptability on a dataset of potato plants’ photos gathered across diverse areas in Pakistan. The models are assessed using performance criteria such computational efficiency, accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score. Random Forest model having 97% accuracy outperforms the other ML models in identifying plant disease. The suggested approach provides a practical, affordable, and effective way to identify diseases in a timely manner, allowing farmers to make informed decisions to lower crop losses. The aim of the study is to highlight how ML has the potential to transform Pakistani agriculture, enhancing food security and promoting long-term economic prosperity.

articleTitle: Wearable Sensor-Based Activity Recognition over Statistical Features Selection and MLP Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Supervising and examining the physical activities of different individuals by using wireless sensors is beneficial in favor of recognizing postural positioning and moving actions in the everyday ambiance. Accelerometers have been exercised in intelligent environments to identify human activities for many years. Using these accelerometer sensors and human activity recognition systems, people going through many sicknesses and illnesses can be proficiently scrutinized, and thus remedial medication can be dispensed in a well-timed approach. In this research paper, a naïve, and intricate technique founded on certain time domain features on the way to classify the physical activities is suggested. Feature extraction is a momentous step in HAR, and in this study, six statistical features were obtained from the preprocessed data. To further optimize the feature set, the Binary Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) was integrated. Further, a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) was utilized for activity recognition to distinguish between the six activity classes. MLP has the advantage of finding non-linear patterns in data, the algorithm possesses powerful features of reducing overfitting in the data and good generality. It also offers resistance to noises usually experienced in the sensor data. Experimental results evaluated that the proposed framework achieved 87.14% recognition accuracy. This validates that the suggested framework can be used to observe physical activities and discriminate between healthy and unhealthy patients.

articleTitle: Optimized Nonlinear Control Approaches for Effective Bone Cancer Treatment
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: This research addresses novel approaches for efficient disease management by using sophisticated control techniques to solve the difficult problem of synchronizing symmetric bones in the human body for the treatment of bone cancer. Sliding mode control and supertwisting sliding mode control are the main controllers under investigation. These controllers were selected because to their ability to withstand uncertainties and disruptions that are present in the dynamic behavior of bone cancer. Gain tuning, a critical aspect of controller design, is optimized using a genetic algorithm, ensuring optimal performance and stability. A comprehensive comparison between SMC and STSMC highlights the superiority of STSMC due to its chattering-free nature, robustness against disturbances, and finite-time stability. Furthermore, the practical applicability of the proposed controllers is validated through real-time implementation using the C2000 Delfino and MCU F28379D Launchpad.

articleTitle: Aging and Corrosion of Aluminum Conductor Caused by Fireproof Mud in a Simulated Cable Trench
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Fireproof mud, a commonly used material in the power and construction industries for sealing and plugging, can unexpectedly accelerate the aging and corrosion of aluminum cables when in direct contact. Despite its prevalent use, limited research has investigated the effects of fireproof mud on aluminum cables. This research focuses on the impact of fireproof mud on aluminum cables, whose application has not been given a comprehensive study despite being widely used in the power as well as construction sectors. By conducting a 2000-hour experimental study in a simulated cable trench, examining the impact of water-based, oil-based, and sealant fire mud on aluminum cables under multiple stress conditions. A comprehensive assessment framework, including visual inspections, electrical insulation resistance measurements, Conductor Insulation Resistance and physical mass loss calculations. Furthermore, a recommendation procedure for corrosion prevention is presented, providing guidelines for enhancing the durability and reliability of electrical infrastructure.

articleTitle: Human-Human Interaction Recognition Using Mask R-CNN and Multi-Class SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Computer vision systems face significant challenges in human-human interaction recognition in dynamic environments, particularly with cluttered backgrounds. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that leverages OpenPose for accurate keypoint detection and Mask R-CNN, pre-trained on the COCO dataset, for precise human segmentation-chosen for their robustness in handling occlusions and complex interactions. To optimize the extracted features, we apply Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) for dimensionality reduction and class separation, ensuring efficient classification using a multi-class support vector machine (SVM). By utilizing these pre-trained models, our system achieves high accuracy with a reduced feature set, demonstrating that excellent performance can be achieved without extensive retraining. We classify six distinct interaction types-including handshaking, pushing, kicking, and punching-while addressing challenges such as fast motion and interaction complexity within the dataset. The system achieves competitive accuracy on the UT Interaction dataset (89.1% on Set 1, 86.6% on Set 2) and demonstrates computational efficiency, making it scalable for real-world applications like public surveillance.

articleTitle: Innovative Wire Cutting Automation: Reducing Material Waste and Human Error
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Wires of different lengths are often utilized for a range of applications in industries and daily life, from manufacturing to electrical installations. However, several issues affect traditional wire-cutting techniques, such as high labor costs, time-consuming, inaccuracy, inefficiency, and safety hazards. Incorrect cutting, wire wastage, and higher expenses for production are the results of traditional manual cutting procedures. These conventional approaches are unfit for the high precision requirements of the current world since they are not only labour intensive but also prone to errors and inconsistencies. These limitations call for an Automated Wire Cutting Machine that incorporates an embedded system with a microcontroller-based control unit, stepper motor-driven wire feeding, and a linear actuator for precise cutting. This machine design allows users to input wire lengths and quantities via a touchscreen interface, ensuring fully automated cutting. Key components, including the stepper motor, cutting mechanism, and touch display for input, work in harmony to ensure accuracy across a wide range of wire lengths. Testing showed that the machine achieved over 97% accuracy in cutting operations, saving labor hours and reducing cutting time while greatly enhancing safety. This automated system offers a scalable, cost-effective solution, enabling industries such as manufacturing, automotive assembly, and electrical installations to operate more efficiently, precisely, and sustainably.

articleTitle: Robust Machine Learning Approach to Plant Species Classification for Sustainable Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Sustaining resilient agricultural practices is essential for the overall yield because it guarantees both economic stability and food supplies. By incorporating Zero-Shot learning into a strong leaf classification architecture, our method meets this demand. We optimized an AI-powered four-step categorization process using the Bee Colony Algorithm. To pre-process, segment, extract features from, and classify leaf image data, zero-shot learning is employed. Pre-processing, which includes histogram equalization and contrast stretching, is followed by morphological segmentation. In feature extraction, two methods are used: Harris corner detection and SURF (Speeded Up Robust Features). Zero-Shot learning for classification is optimized using the Bee Colony Algorithm. At 92.73 % accuracy, the suggested method surpasses out previous methods like CNN and SVM, suggesting that it has the potential to enhance crop quality and disease control in agriculture.

articleTitle: Optimized Nonlinear Control Strategies for Hybrid Electric Vehicles Integrating Photoelectrochemical and Photovoltaic Cells with Fuel Cells, Batteries, and Supercapacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are gaining traction due to the depletion of fossil fuel and natural gas reserves. To counteract the harmful impacts of global warming and greenhouse gas emissions, adopting renewable energy sources is crucial. This study presents a novel optimized nonlinear control strategy for a hybrid energy storage system (HESS) designed for hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), The HESS incorporates fuel cells (FC), batteries, supercapacitors, and hybrid photoelectrochemical and photovoltaic cells (HPEV). These power sources are connected through a DC-DC power converter, which subsequently powers a DC-AC inverter and an electric motor. The proposed controller utilizes a supertwisting sliding mode control (STSMC) approach to achieve precise DC bus voltage regulation, efficient current tracking for the energy sources, and ensure the closed-loop system's global asymptotic stability. The gain parameters of the STSMC are fine-tuned using the genetic algorithm (GA) to enhance system performance. Furthermore, maximum power point tracking (MPPT) for the HPEV system is implemented via the perturb and observe (P&O) method. The effectiveness of the optimized HESS is evaluated through MATLAB/Simulink simulations, utilizing data from an extra-urban driving cycle. Additionally, hardware-in-the-loop (C-HIL) testing validates the simulation results, confirming the system's performance in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Supervised Learning Approaches for Vibration Analysis and Anomaly Detection in Rotating Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Safety and reliability are crucial for modern systems and technologies. This paper presents an approach for real-time anomaly detection in rotating machines using vibration analysis and machine learning algorithms for predictive maintenance. Rotating machines such as motors, engines, gearboxes and turbines are widely used systems and faults in these systems can result in complete shutdowns. Preventing unexpected downtime while ensuring equipment reliability and safety is essential. In this context, anomaly detection plays a vital role in monitoring the healthy operation of rotating machines. A test-bed was designed to generate datasets for both balanced (healthy) and unbalanced (faulty) motor conditions. The experimental setup consists of a three-phase induction motor, a signal acquisition system (Raspberry Pi), a vibration sensor (MPU6050) and a coupling system capable of adjusting motor balance. Supervised machine learning algorithms, Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Random Forest (RF) were applied to classify and detect anomalies in the collected datasets. A grid search algorithm was employed for hyperparameter tuning of the SVM and RF models. The proposed technique achieved a maximum accuracy of approximately 98% using SVM and 100% using the RF algorithm leveraging nine optimally selected temporal features.

articleTitle: Enhanced Domestic Short-Term Load Forecasting Using a Hybrid Deep Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: There are numerous challenges associated with operating today's electrical grids such as: shift in consumer preferences, the increased utilization of the renewable power sources and the need for load regulation. It remains important that way because without good electrical load management short-term load forecasting (STLF) helps in improving the effectiveness of the grid system. This paper seeks to make a comparison of two complex deep learning algorithms which are Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Network Bidirectional LSTM (CNN-BiLSTM) in the context of predicting consumption of energy in residential houses. The Bi-LSTM stands for the bidirectional LSTM; such an arrangement is more effective than typical LSTM displays as it makes temporal dependencies in both layers like as the backward and forward respectively. On the other hand, the CNN-BiLSTM model comprises of CNN layers used in extracting features of data and Bi-LSTM used in handling spatial and temporal features. For the purpose of an evaluation, the results of presented models have been compared with other conventional approaches by using the measures like Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). The results found out that the CNN-BiLSTM model indicates improved precision and is better at predicting the energy usage patterns as compared to the Bi-LSTM and traditional predictive models. The paper also present the direction for the enhanced load forecast using the complex structure of neural networks and the future directions to work upon the improvement of load forecast in the energy management system.

articleTitle: Detection of Parkinson's Disease from Voice Signals Using Explainable Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease have presented one of the major health challenges facing the world today, especially with the increasing prevalence seen with increasing aging populations. In this regard, AI has been emerged as a promising method for early detection and intervention. Therefore, in the paper, an explainable approach for deep learning in voice recordings toward diagnosing Parkinson's disease is presented. It uses a modified Attention ResNet18 architecture with Squeeze-and-Excitation blocks and utilizes Mel-Spectrogram features obtained from audio signals. Grad-CAM, Integrated Gradients, and LIME were used to provide the explanations generated by the model during the classification process. Experimental results presented an accuracy of 97.8<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> for classification, thus demonstrating the ability of Explainable AI to detect non-invasive PD.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of a Six Degrees of Freedom Parallel Mechanism Based Robotic Machining Bed
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: In precision manufacturing, the stability of the machining element is of utmost importance, and it is provided by the machining beds. To enhance the functionality and dexterity of these machining beds, parallel manipulators are integrated with them. Although these manipulators offer more flexibility and execution of various complex tasks, still guaranteeing their optimal performance is a challenge. To overcome this issue, the present research suggests an optimization technique employing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) which improves the performance of the proposed robotic machining bed by minimizing its conditioning index and increasing the overall workspace. PSO is a stochastic searching algorithm inspired by the concept of fish schooling or murmuration of birds. The outcomes of the research provide an optimized model of robotic machining bed which leads towards accurate machining operations and efficient precision manufacturing facilities.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation in Cooperative NOMA: Opportunities and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The radio access technology keeps users connected to communication networks anywhere and anytime in Fifth Generation and beyond wireless communication systems (b5G). Future radio access technologies incorporate major wireless communication system parameters, like huge data rates, massive connectivity, high energy efficiency, very low latency, etc. Hence, there is a need to bring revolutionary changes in the present radio access technologies (RATs). The employment of 5G and beyond technologies aim to provide better throughput, lower latency, excellent user connectivity and quality of service, and reliability. Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) techniques are employed to allow users to share the same time-frequency blocks. NOMA can support huge data rates, massive connectivity and promises user fairness. The user capacity of NOMA can be enhanced by integrating it with the cooperative relay networks, that provide enhanced spectral efficiency, energy efficiency and user connectivity. This article presents the detailed review of resource allocation techniques in Cooperative NOMA (CNOMA) with discussion about the challenges in implementing CNOMA in multi-user communications system.

articleTitle: Detecting Lung Nodule Malignancy Using CNN-Based Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: This study focuses on the development of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based deep learning model to detect cancerous lung nodules from computed-tomography (CT) scans. Timely identification of lung cancer is essential in improving survival rates, as it remains a leading cause of global cancer-related mortality. CNN models improve medical image analysis by automating the classification process to offer increased diagnostic accuracy. A custom-built CNN model is employed to distinguish between benign and malignant lung nodules using CT scans from the Kaggle's Data Science Bowl 2017 dataset. Our model reached a 92% accuracy in data classification. The findings show that this CNN-driven approach excels previous techniques in identifying lung nodule malignancy, allowing more precise diagnoses, and improved patient outcomes. Future research should explore using cascaded algorithms and leveraging multiple datasets to enhance prediction accuracy and generalization of malignancy, as well as reduce overfitting impact.

articleTitle: RGB-D Scene Classification: A Unified Framework with Vision Transformers and Contextual Models
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Indoor scene classification poses a significant challenge, crucial for advancements in robotics, augmented reality, and smart environments. This paper presents an innovative model designed for classifying indoor scenes using RGB-D images. The model seamlessly integrates unsupervised segmentation, Vision Transformers (VT), convolutional neural networks, and conditional random fields. The workflow starts with segmenting the RGB-D data through the DBSCAN algorithm, followed by feeding the segmented images into a Vision Transformer for feature extraction. The VT features two branches: one dedicated to capturing fine-grained local patch representations and another focused on modeling long-range dependencies through self-attention mechanisms. The resulting features are then processed by a ResNet-18 architecture for multi-object classification, enhancing the understanding of the scene's content. Ultimately, the classified objects and contextual information from the VT's relation modeling branch are merged within a Conditional Random Field framework for comprehensive scene classification. Testing on the NYU-Dv2 and SUN RGB-D datasets reveals that our approach significantly outperforms existing techniques in accurately classifying diverse indoor environments. This methodology sets the stage for enhanced scene understanding, with promising applications in robotics, augmented reality, and smart environments.
